Currently we have been using a work-around (not very scalable) in Estonia, where we gather all these orders in one file and deduct commissions from drivers manually. Although it's not scalable, it's fairly easy to do since every driver pays us 20% commission. In 2 other Baltic countries the situation is very different - different fleets pay different commissions and even worse: 1 driver might pay 3 different types of commissions, depending on the payment method (i.e 0.61€ per cash trip with VAT; 15% with Adyen; 12.1% if corporate payment etc) meaning that the manual switch in admin triggering the charge of correct commission would save us time and money. It would save us time, because currently someone has to create a Jira ticket for us, one of us has to figure out what is the correct commission they should've paid if price review is closed with 0€ (since we don't want to charge client's card if they paid in cash), go and deduct it and then reply to the CS agent. It will save us money because on many markets deductions are not done or even considered when price review has been closed with 0 when client pays in cash for a ride which was initially ordered with in-app payments.
resolved as we disabled the auto payment switching.

2. Manually create an additional cash payment with the same value as the original in-app payment

This way the commission amounts should be correct and it is clear what happened.

For me all the cases described in the pdf boil down to 2 problems really:
1. Very fast change of multipliers on drivers map
2. Very different multipliers in points several meters from each other in Riders/User app

I will try explain to explain why both of this problems happen , and how we can fix them or already fixing.

*1. Fast change of multipliers.*

Speed of multiplier changes is defined by 2 factors:
   1. How often we recalculate city state (all the multipliers across a given city) - gathering  input data(number of searches and drivers) and running algorithm to figure out the multipliers. Currently recalculation happens every 10 seconds.
   2. How aggressively recalculation algorithm reacts on input data 

Recalculation algorithm used currently in Tallinn is pretty simple:
   1. For each hexagonal cell in the city count searches and drivers in certain radius. Subtract drivers from searches
   2. If difference is more than certain threshold (2) increase multiplier if not decrease it
   3. In case of increasing value is calculated by formula  new_multiplier = smooth_function(prev_multiplier_value, rising_speed  * (diff - prev_diff)). Decreasing = smooth_function(prev_multiplier_value, falling_speed * (diff - prev_diff))
   4. Smooth function tries to smooth the change a bit.
   4. Size of hex cell, radius are from where the data is collected, rising and falling speed are configurable parameters which can be tuned in Admin per city

So looking at historical data for the time described in the pdf - Tallinn, 27.06.2018 16.08- 16.30. Configuration parameters - hex radius - ~400m, hex cell centers are spread approximately 800m from each other; data radius - 1500m, rising speed - 0.015 per second, falling - 0.01 per second. 
Location of pdf examples is in Tallinn Old City which is covered pretty much by a single cell (you can see it from very top/right screenshot of drivers app). Some data samples for this cell:
*    16:09:16 - multiplier - 1.0 - searches: 5, drivers: 3 
*   16:10:26 - multiplier: 1.5, searches: 6, drivers: 3 => smooth_function(1.0, 0.015 * 60 secs * ((6 - 3) - (5 - 3))) => smooth_function(1.0 , +0.9) => 1.5
 *  16:11:36 - multiplier - 1.0, searches - 4, drivers - 3 => smooth_function(1.5, 0.01 * 60 secs * ((4 - 3) - (6 - 3))) => smooth_function(1.5,  -1.2) => 1.0

From these samples it’s visible that change in searches/drivers difference by 1-2 in either direction causes multiplier to increase or decrease by 0.5 over 1 minute. And thats because smoothing slightly reduces it. Without smoothing its +0.9 and -1.2. 

Clearly rising and falling speed configurations are too aggressive.

*Possible improvements/fixes:*
  1. If fast changes of multipliers is really a problem - easy short term fix is to reduce rising/falling configurations for the city. 
  2. City state calculation frequency can be reduced. But thats will just reduce amount of updates not the speed of multipliers changes. So if currently we have 6 recalculations per minute and multiplier changes over a minute will look   like 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 1.4 1.5. In case of frequency of once per minute this will be 1.0 ….. 1.5. Multiplier change stays same time wise we just have less data sampling points. Another drawback is that frequency can’t be changed per city - this is global parameter affecting all the cities.
 3. New, more efficient algorithm -  this is long term solution. Thats what we are working on with Data Science team currently.

*2. Different multipliers in points several meters from each other.*
Pdf examples cover a case when user stays in same hex cell with same multiplier (theoretically) but get different values while moving several meters around. 
This problem is caused not by Dynamic Pricing per se but by the way we lock prices for user. The first time user gets his/location - the price is locked for 5 minutes and the price lock works in range of several meters. If location is moved user gets another price lock based on current Dynamic Pricing multiplier. So if user moves the cursor - he locks price in those small cells and freezes multiplier/price there. 
Even if Dynamic Pricing continuously recalculates multipliers - regions where user has price lock are not affected until they expire after 5 mins. 
Thats why user gets several different multipliers in slightly different locations and those multipliers are not correlated with Drivers view.

*Possible improvements/fixes*
 1. Short term - Reducing  price expiration lock from 5 mins to lets say 2 mins in combination with slowing down Dynamic 
 Pricing multiplier changes should make this problem less noticeable.
 2. Long term - Redoing algorithm of how we lock prices for user - this what Im planning to work  on soon.

*Additional comments:*
1. Strictly speaking comparison of multipliers returned by Rider/User app and heat map displayed is not correct. First of all, it’s technically impossible to do them exactly the same. Second - future direction is to completely separate Drivers demand map and multipliers returned to users. Obvious example here is user trying to get an order from suburbs and receiving high multiplier while drivers map ignoring this area to avoid moving drivers to bad locations.
2. No matter how smart Dynamic Pricing algorithm we going to have in future - human monitoring and intervention will be required. Its already impossible for dev team to monitor and tune ~40 cities configurations. IMHO this implies that city teams should take bigger part in Dynamic Pricing maintenance and tuning.  Currently this doesn’t seem to be the case. From my side Im ready to provide whatever support/training/documentation necessary.

Overtime is paid at x1.5 for hours worked over 45 hours per week, this is as per the Basic Conditions of Employment Act (BCEA).

Shift employees - those who's working days are any of the seven days of the week as paid at x0.5 for Sundays and at x1.0 for pubic holidays - if these hours are included in your contracted 40 hour week.

Bamboo shows always +*current*+ annual leave days balance. That means that even if you have planned your annual leave in the future, today you still have pending 20,3 days. The issue seems to be caused by regions that span outside the cities. The current flow is the following:
# "/findCategoriesOverview" tries to look up the region/city/country by search location
# it finds that location falls into region
# it looks up the city data for that region and fetches all search categories for that city
# categories are passed to "/internal/createPricing"
# it compares the city for each search category with the city for the search location, but it sees that location doesn't fall into any available city (null case) or falls into another city (city ID mismatch)

There are two potential solutions for this:
# Fix regions configuration: they are not supposed to span outside of cities.
# Improve city/region matching algorithm:
  * match by country first
  * then match by city, but only among cities for matched country
  * finally match for region, but only among regions that belong to the matched city

With this strategy we will either match the appropriate city first, in which case the different (appropriate) set of search categories will be returned, or we won't match by city at all, in which case the region won't even be considered and AREA_NOT_SERVICED code will be returned.

An employer, when giving the notice of termination of an employment contract during a probation period, does not have a duty to indicate the cause for such notice.

1) Is the annex relevant for morning(around 9AM-5PM) and evening (around 2.30PM-11PM) shifts as well? Or should we sign a new annex?
This annex is applicable to the abovementioned shift work, but please note that in accordance with the Article 139, Paragraph 1 of the Latvian Labour Law the duration of the shift shall not exceed 8 hours (the break is not included), providing that it is not a night work. If an employee works more than 8 hours, the employer and employee shall agree on aggregate working time.
2) (5) An employer has a duty to familiarise employees with the shift schedules not later than one month before they come into effect. - is one month notice mandatory or we can have it shorter if we would make a new contract annex? Would it be legal to make a shorter notice?
 
In accordance with Article 139, Paragraph 5 of the Latvian Labour Law one month notice is mandatory and it is not allowed to shorten it by the agreement of the employer and employee.

Here is the formal answer from Labour Law: An unused part of holiday shall be transferred to the next calendar year. The claim for annual holiday expires within one year as of the end of the calendar year for which the holiday is calculated. So 2018 annual holiday will expire on 31.12.2019. But if he/she takes her holiday during 2019 then the calculation is done so that 2018 year vacation days will be used as first.

Query used for analysis:

SELECT o.country,
[o.id|http://o.id],
ot.driver_id,
ROUND((SQRT(POWER(datc.lat-da.lat,2)\+POWER(datc.lng-da.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) as distance_between_driver_accepted_and_driver_arrived_to_client,
ROUND((SQRT(POWER(datc.lat-o.lat,2)\+POWER(datc.lng-o.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) as distance_between_taxi_ordered_here_and_driver_arrived_to_client,
ROUND((SQRT(POWER(cdns.lat-o.lat,2)\+POWER(cdns.lng-o.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) as distance_between_client_did_not_show_and_taxi_ordered_here,
ROUND((SQRT(POWER(cc.lat-o.lat,2)\+POWER(cc.lng-o.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) as distance_between_client_cancelled_and_taxi_ordered_here,
ot.distance as pickup_distance,
pr.price/r.rate as price
FROM company_order as o
LEFT JOIN company_order_try as ot ON ot.order_id=[o.id|http://o.id] AND o.connection_id=ot.connection_id
LEFT JOIN company_order_try_state_log as da ON da.order_try_id=[ot.id|http://ot.id] AND da.connection_id=ot.connection_id AND da.to_state='driver_accepted'
LEFT JOIN company_order_try_state_log as datc ON datc.order_try_id=[ot.id|http://ot.id] AND datc.connection_id=ot.connection_id AND datc.to_state='driver_arrived_to_client'
LEFT JOIN company_order_try_state_log as cdns ON cdns.order_try_id=[ot.id|http://ot.id] AND cdns.connection_id=ot.connection_id AND cdns.to_state='client_did_not_show'
LEFT JOIN company_order_try_state_log as cc ON cc.order_try_id=[ot.id|http://ot.id] AND cc.connection_id=ot.connection_id AND cc.to_state='client_cancelled'
LEFT JOIN company_order_try_price_row as pr ON pr.connection_id=ot.connection_id AND pr.order_try_id=[ot.id|http://ot.id]
LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates as r ON r.currency=ot.price_currency AND DATE(r.valid_on)=DATE(ot.created)
WHERE o.created BETWEEN '2018-10-22' AND '2018-10-28 23:59:59'
AND ot.state IN ('client_cancelled','client_did_not_show')
AND o.payment_method_type IN ('corporate','adyen','paystack','zooz','mpesa','corporate_ext','emt')
\-\-AND ot.state='finished'
\-\-AND ot.distance > 200
\-\-AND ot.driver_id=652677
\-\-AND pr.type='cancellation_fee'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9
HAVING
\-\-ROUND((SQRT(POWER(datc.lat-da.lat,2)\+POWER(datc.lng-da.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) < 0.1
ROUND((SQRT(POWER(datc.lat-o.lat,2)\+POWER(datc.lng-o.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) > 0.3
AND (ROUND((SQRT(POWER(cdns.lat-o.lat,2)\+POWER(cdns.lng-o.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) > 0.3
OR ROUND((SQRT(POWER(cc.lat-o.lat,2)\+POWER(cc.lng-o.lng,2))\*111)\*1.0,1) > 0.3)

the labour law states the following:

Section 172. Compensation Schedule

1. As a rule wages shall be divided into *two parts (advance and remaining pay) and paid to employees twice a month with an interval not to exceed sixteen days*. Wages for employees whose salaries are calculated over a one-year period must be paid not less than once a month,

2. Other terms for the payment of wages may also be stipulated in collective agreements and employment contracts.

3. If a payday falls on a holiday or weekend, payment shall be made the day prior.

4. Should an employee quit, all payments due him shall be paid in fall on the day that he quits.

5. If payments are delayed through the fault of the employer and this has not already resulted in a grievance by the employee, the employee shall be paid an additional one percent of his salary for each day the payment is delayed. If the delay has resulted in a grievance, it shall be resolved pursuant to the guidelines in the section on Labour Disputes herein.

6. If an employee's record book is not issued within the time determined in Subsection 3 of Section 87 of this Code and the delay is the fault of the employer, the employee must be paid an average salary for the entire period of time during which he was not hired.

Note: The phrase "delay is the fault of the employer" used in this Section shall mean non-payment of an employee's salary over the period in question due to salaries not having been calculated within the fixed time, salaries not having been withdrawn from an authorized bank and financial and accounting operations not having been conducted in time, as well as in cases depending directly on the employer's will and capabilities. This procedure shall not apply in cases when an employer is not able to pay employee salaries on time due to a bank's mishandling of operations regarding funds when said employer is a client of the bank, due to the bankruptcy of the bank, or due to non-payment by another employer for work performed or services rendered, etc., which do not depend on the employer.

Hey Kristjan, 

I have been doing some reading/research into your question and found some interesting articles (which I will link) that liken company email to personal data under GDPR. Certainly, as a question of privacy and GDPR, this should be addressed with Guido.

My impression is that emails clearly stating the name of the employee and/or which are used to represent the employee directly (not just info@taxify for example) would count as personal data and need to be processed in compliance with GDPR. However, like with any GDPR action, with 'legitimate purpose' could be used to justify processing (like for disciplinary purposes). I think that we will need to evaluate the risks (DPO should do a risk impact assessment) and decide internally our policy in what cases this action would be appropriate. We can then draft some broad version of this into our new internal employee privacy notice. As personal data, I would understand that the employee would have the right to request to be forgotten. Though we could deny this for some time where need exists, we wouldn't be able to store such information indefinitely. (though again, confirm with Guido).

Sorry its not so black-and-white. Law rarely is, but I hope that gives some kind of an idea about how we can move forward with making a policy for this.

* Cross City Tunnel

[https://australia-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/48925885/50688673]
[https://australia-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/48926306/50689179] (wtf Google...)
* New M4
** omittable
[https://australia-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/48927588/50690763]
[https://australia-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/48927928/50691208]

Not predicted, encountered:

* Lane Cove Tunnel
** driver's fault (fraud?) \- took a longer and more expensive route
[https://australia-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/48927657/50690847]
[https://australia-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/48927498/50690659]

[https://australia-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/48928580/50692014]

----
So far it seems that we might have a couple of problems with toll roads themselves, but the rest is mostly detours or Google suggesting more expensive routes. The latter can be hopefully fixed by sending some extra params to Maps API to encounter for toll roads.

I think it also makes sense to see what’s the difference (meter price \- upfront) for the last group, since it seems to be shifted to the positive side, i.e. drivers taking more expensive routes, maybe there’s some fraud element there. Also weird cases are where Google seems to suggest very similar road going through the same toll roads that were added in the end, but price prediction just doesn’t contain them for some reason, and it’s pretty hard to investigate why, if this becomes an issue, we might want to add some extra logging in price prediction maybe?

Lastly, I’d also like to gather some statistics on the percentage of each type of mismatches relative to total number of trips with toll roads to estimate the impact and to monitor the ratio after we configure Maps API requests appropriately.

Hi Zandile,

Thank you for submitting your request. 

This is actually a consideration we have to make often when reviewing what local privacy law looks like in all of our countries and actually the answer is rather complicated. We use local legal counsel to assist us in assuring that our business practices are in conformity with local privacy requirements and to localize our terms and conditions where needed and as we see appropriate. However, when it comes to the Taxify app and its operation, as the app belongs to an Estonian company, it provided under Estonian law (defined in the introduction to our terms for riders and section 9). Additionally, GDPR is considered to be the 'gold standard' in data protection so it is safe to say it is better to be over compliant by following the terms of GDPR. Thus, GDPR is the primary source of law in relation to the Taxify app, though of course this could be debated be local regulators. 

Sorry that its not such a black and white answer, law rarely is. Any more detailed questions related to GDPR can be best answered by our data protection officer Guido, but I hope this helped to give you a quick overview of his the laws interact.

Hi, we are building an insurance offer to help drivers in their job.
- Loi El Khomri has been into force since January 2018 and forces platforms to pay a part of insurance coverage in case a driver doing more than ca 5K€ revenue yearly on a platform asks for it.
- Uber has released last year an insurance cover in France on Health, Injury, Disability and death, complying with the law El Khomri.

- We want to offer a much more narrow scoped insurance (accidents) but covering more, in case they have driven more. The offer is: in case of accident during a Txfy ride, the driver would be eligible for a daily payment up to 30 days of the average daily revenue made on Txfy over the past 2 months. This should be a great offer to drivers to trust us more and it will enable us to also reward best ones.

Also, keep in mind we will most likely decrease base prices soon in Paris, and increase the commission rate in a few weeks. The insurance coverage should also help us offer some additional value at the same time we lower some dimensions.

Countries usually agree in their bilateral tax treaties that rewards & prizes are taxed only by the country of residence (source country forfeits taxing right). This is expressed in both EE-NL and EE-CZ agreement (art. 22). For practical purposes I’d suggest the team chooses one as representative and recipient of the payment. This person will have to ask for a ‘certificate of tax residence’ from his/ her local tax office and send it to us. Then we can make the payment in full (i.e. w/o deducting the 20% income tax otherwise due). Alternatively, we make the payment immediately, deduct the tax and they claim it back from the EE tax authorities.

Hey, I took a quick look and 12/16 cases are most probably due to the fact that the source or destination is inside or very close to the edge of inner or outer toll road polygon. This just means that sometimes drivers take a small detour and toll road actually counts in the end because they took a different route from what Google suggested. The difference with the suggested route might be really small and barely noticeable, but unfortunately our current toll roads mechanism doesn't handle this case very well, and frankly it wasn't designed to handle this "hackish city borders" case :)

AFAIR, the plan was to remove the toll road hack altogether anytime soon, since we have an experiment with dynamic pricing running in Kyiv which is supposed to resolve this issue and be a dedicated replacement for "low value driver rides", if I may. [~accountid:557058:d7e9b4c4-963d-4589-8f8a-035efd1d2ced] please correct me if I'm wrong. Hence I wouldn't spend too much time (if any) on handling those issues, they should go away pretty soon.

As for the other cases:
* https://europe-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/214568801
the feature was released on 03.12 in Kyiv, so this order didn't have the functionality yet :)
* https://europe-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/234194875/250790805
here the pricing switched to regular because the ride was >40km and toll road is included as it normally would be
* https://europe-admin.taxify.eu/order/Orders/order/222389260
similar case, >40km -> regular pricing, but also if you look closer you'll see that a couple of points were skipped due to GPS issues and the inner toll road zone didn't count as crossed, so this is a usual toll roads GPS mismatch issue

P.S. This makes me think that maybe we could differentiate (in admin, on order page) between initial type of pricing shown as a prediction to rider and final one, so that it would be easier to identify cases like >40km or recalculation, it's not that obvious from the price log.

Yes, in essence this is what it is referring to, that the consumer’s right of refund as is upheld by regulation in the EU related to product and services. Transport services however are excluded from the scope of the directive, so we are clarifying to the rider that this regulation is not applicable. 

*Article 27:*
_Transport services cover passenger transport and transport of goods. Passenger transport should be excluded from the scope of this Directive as it is already subject to other Union legislation or, in the case of public transport and taxis, to regulation at national level. However, the provisions of this Directive protecting consumers against excessive fees for the use of means of payment or against hidden costs should apply also to passenger transport contracts. In relation to transport of goods and car rental which are services, consumers should benefit from the protection afforded by this Directive, with the exception of the right of withdrawal._

For more reading if you are interested you can review the directive here: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32011L0083&rid=1

Hi Nonso, 

I have reviewed this issue and also coordinated with our in-house insurance expert Armin and in summary have concluded that ultimately this will come down to a business decision on our side as there is no applicable insurance claim against us here. 

From a legal standpoint, there is not obligation for Taxify Ghana or Taxify OU to make any payments in relation to a damages or insurance claim as we are in no way at fault or party to the accident. Remember, that as we do NOT provide transportation service, we are not party to the relationship between the Driver and Rider, and thus resulting claims that arise from this service should be resolved between them directly. Further more, Taxify Ghana would never be the party for them to even attempt to claim as liable since its function is not related to the licensing of the app. Thus, if we do feel that it would be a good business choice to cover the cost of the phone and are not concerned that it could cause a precedent for cases going forward, then we could do so. However, if we do proceed this way then I would advise that we abide by our T&Cs and not agree to compensation of more than 500 euros at most.

Personally I think what ever decision we make needs to be run by our local counsel and that local counsel needs to be made aware of the function of our businesses (Taxify Ghana vs Taxify Kenya)(Platform not Transportation service provider) so that they can advise us accordingly. 

For your own reference, the following T&C sections explain our relationship with users in relation to damage and liability:

*Rider*

*6.2* We only organize transportation, we are not a service provider.
*6.5* No damage to property will be covered by us.
*6.6* Regardless of whether liability is accepted or not, we limit all claims to 500 euros. 
*6.7* Indemnity of Taxify.
*9* Relationship is governed by Estonian law as we are the provider of the platform.

*Driver*

*4.1/10.1* Confirms that the driver is the provider of transportation services and is thus liable. 
*12.5* Liability of the Driver in relation to claims by the rider

_Of course, if using these points to elaborating our standpoint to a driver/rider, please don't copy and paste as they are worded here since this is very simplified and just for internal reference._ 

I think one learning experience that can be taken from this case is educating our team on how and what we release to customers in terms of describing 1. our relationships with drivers and; 2. our insurance coverage. Driver/Rider price separation would require 3 things:
1. Separate price columns in order/order_try - this is already there - *price * and *ride_price*. There is a legacy *client_extra_fees* which is a difference of the 2 above. It should be removed/deprecated
2. Separate surge multipliers for rider and driver in price_lock(?). Rider multiplier is there - addition is of driver one is relatively easy. The only question is when we define the driver multiplier - at same time as the rider one or later when we know the driver already (when order_try gets created).
3. Add support of drivers and riders price components. There are 3 possibilities:
 1. Additional price_row table for driver with copy of the rider components
 2. Additional table for driver which has only delta/difference between rider and driver components
 3. Add a column to existing order_try_price_row table which will define where price_row belongs - to driver, to rider or both
 
I would estimate effort for doing this  as ~1 week dev time

As you have marked the country "Estonia", I assume that the changes are done in Estonia.

Unfortunately you cannot put these persons on an additional probation (in Estonia), this is forbidden by the law. 

_Changing the contract conditions during the employment relationship, usually transferring the employee to some other task, is no reason for a new trial period. Prior to transferring the employee to the new position, the employer must evaluate whether they have sufficient knowledge, skills, qualification and experience to manage at the new position. If the employee does not cope at the new position due to insufficient skills, non-suitability for the position or incapability to adapt, the employment contract can be terminated extraordinarily on legally prescribed conditions._

The solution can be:
a) They will start on their new position with their new salary right away (with proper contract and new salary) and without probation period
b) Or they will have the same CS contract, no position change or salary change will follow, but they will do 50% of CS and 50% new position tasks during few months and after you are sure that they can manage with the new positions, we can formalise it with the new contract and salary (and without probation period).
You can pay them during the test time a small bonus for doing more skilled work than CS.

The last option has to be agreed with the employee and they have to know the exact terms. Also the possibility if they do not succeed, that their position will fully be CS and no salary changes do not apply anymore after the test period is over.

* Term is one year and exit is easy for both parties with one month's notice BUT as the fees paid are non-refundable is this smart? This means they could just take the money and cut very easily. * 3 refers to other letters which should be accounted with this agreement. Rather, should the agreement not now cover all terms? *  Finances: The pricing structure in both the agreement and the counter-proposal is very confusing. Thank you for submitting. Andrius and I have recently had a discussion on this topic relating to the right to block drivers without notice, but this case is different significantly in substance so I will elaborate further.

In this case the main issues are blocking vs. termination. I agree where allegations are made against the drive we need to take them seriously and blocking the driver is a logical first step. However, termination of our agreement with the driver (ie. permanent blocking) is something that really should be done with more justification/proof and blocking should be a temporary step during the investigation. 

Some examples of this justification/proof for permanent block could be:
-police report
-reoccurring rider complaints (like with low rating hard blocks)
-evidence (video, photo, etc.)

Ultimately, it will be a business decision in terms of how this case is resolved but I would highlight that to a judge the permanent termination of the agreement with one unverified complaint will probably not stand. It would be challenging to justify the action which our team took under terms and conditions to permanently block the driver in this case. We are not the judge and jury, and though we have every reason to believe our rider, essentially the driver has a point in saying that we have acted without proof or reason. 

As a review, the clause we use to unilaterally block or terminate a driver is 13.3.:
 _Taxify or Taxify group companies and partners are entitled to immediately terminate the Agreement and block your access to Taxify Platform without giving any advance notice in case you breach the General Terms of Agreement, any applicable laws or regulations, disparage Taxify or Taxify group companies and partners, or *cause harm to Taxify’s brand, reputation or business as determined by Taxify or Taxify group companies and partners in our sole discretion*. In the aforementioned cases, we may, at its own discretion, prohibit you from registering a new Driver account._

I think in such a case the part in bold would be the most relevant justification for us blocking but I still think our business practice in terms of follow up and hard blocking should be carefully considered because it would be hard to state that the bold was reflected in only one unverified incident. Hey Karin!

I have read through. Thank you for reading this yourself, you did hit a number of the big things. Overall this is an agreement in fairly good condition so I will pretty much just highlight to you my main findings/feelings.

*The detailed explanation for you*
* 1.5 gives you a cancellation grace period of 24 hours (assuming you will still pay for work done if there has been any in that period). Just FYI
* 2.1 2.2 I agree, the date is wrong. Clearly, they meant 2020 so that should be changed. I also agree it would be better to have the auto-renewal changed to renewable with the written agreement of both parties or something like this. Also as you have said, an addition stating that at the end of the term the fee will require reconsideration. 
* 3.1 why is this not Annexed? 
* 3.2 they have a third party 'management fee' of 5 %. This seems vague and strange, normal in PR?
* Should add 3.5 that all fees outside of what has been confirmed in annex 1 for the communication product must be mutually agreed and confirmed in writing. 
* 3.3 states that the minimum monthly payment will be 1160 but that this is just a division of the total project cost of 13920. I think this is a little risky as it sets you up for dispute in case of early termination. I would recommend asking for the removal of 3.3 and leaving just that the service and fee for the communication project to be elaborated in Annex 1. I would also recommend making the service fee monthly in the annexed and not just a division of the whole or this could be quite disputable on termination.
* 7.1 should include reference to the contact people for both parties as it does not make sense that it should be as stated in the preamble (in our case Ahto).  Should have the contact of the project leaders inserted here. 
* I agree with your point at 9.1 regarding changing 60 to 30 days. To avoid payment confusion, I think it would be good to add here a point that, "Upon termination of the agreement, payment for the communication product will be resolved by completing the final invoice issued for the previous monthly fee."
* 11.7 is broad. Fine if no user personal data is being given under this agreement? 
* In the annex, just note that the date is wrong again and that you should add in the monthly cost to art 3 (since they will be removed from the main agreement at 3.3)


*Summary to them*
* Please remove section 3.3 and instead add to annex article 1 that we will pay 1160 monthly. We will not require a yearly or total fee in reference. Rather just that the project will continue for 12 months.
* Please check the dates in the agreement and adjust, there are some issues.
* Please change this agreement to have no automatic renewal. It is our preference to renew with mutual agreement at the end of the term. 
* Please move the fee list at 3.1 to the annex.
* Please add to 3.5 that all fees outside of what has been confirmed in annex 1 for the communication product must be mutually agreed and confirmed in writing. 
* Please add contact info for contact people to 7.1 rather than a reference to the preamble. 
* Please change termination from 60 days to 30 in section 9. Also, please add a clarifying point here that "upon termination of the agreement, payment for the communication product will be resolved by completing the final invoice issued for the previous monthly fee."

This with these minor adjustments I do not suspect you will face much resistance but should you need further assistance let me know!

In GDPR perspective we are controllers and any other party who has access to data is processor. GDPR requires to have DPA between controller and processor. Confidentiality is good thig but this word does not every agreement GDPR compliant. This is why:
* controller has to define in detail what data, how and for what purpose is allowed to process
* controller is responsible in area where processor processes data
* processor needs to have processes in place written in GDPR article 12-23, including auditing etc.
* processor is responsible to report on any data breach ASAP
* we as controller are responsible to report to authorities on any data breach in 72h
* GDPR violation is expensive. Fines are 2%,  worst case scenario 4% on annual global GMV.

On a side note (since I have been having the NDA talk with many people this week), I will just quickly review why an NDA is not effective here. Non-disclosure agreements are precontractual agreements which impose confidentiality restrictions on parties prior to them entering a formal agreement. You don't always need an NDA, it just depends how sensitive your precontractual chats are. Once entering a service agreement, you will instead be covered for your partnership moving forward with the clauses in the agreement on confidentiality. Usually, once you enter an agreement, a NDA will be null and void (replaced with the confidentiality clauses) unless otherwise mentioned in the agreement. *NDA's are not to be confused with DPA's*, which are a requirement under the law in the EU to be in place any time you are releasing your companies user data to a third party. Hope that makes this point a bit clearer :)

_Taxify has agreed to share certain confidential information about its Driver Partners with Cheki Nigeria for the purpose of the vehicle financing and acquisition of Driver Partners._ 

We do not and can not share personal information about our drivers with a third party without: a) a service agreement in place; b) Collecting clear and specific driver consent and; c) entering a data processing agreement (DPA) with the party we are disclosing to which must be confirmed and reviewed by our data protection officer (DPO) as all user data in admin is from Taxify ou and covered by GDPR.

There are currently 4 active toll roads which use car tag filters (other filter types are unused):
[https://admin.taxify.eu/toll_roads/roadParameters/edit/207]
[https://admin.taxify.eu/toll_roads/roadParameters/edit/208]
[https://admin.taxify.eu/toll_roads/roadParameters/edit/461]
[https://admin.taxify.eu/toll_roads/roadParameters/edit/425]

After discussion with Femi, it turned out that those filters are indeed being used and will even be extended in the future. The problem is that we can have different vehicle types (with different tags) under the same search category, so it’s rather improbable that we could predict vehicle type accurately during search time.

Femi’s proposal was to always pick the highest price from all available filters, as for riders it won’t result in a significant price difference on average, yet for drivers of SUV (vehicles with higher toll fees) it might be noticeable.

As a side notice, these 4 toll roads are set up in such way that there’s also a fallback price matrix with no filters, therefore we’re able to match toll road with that price matrix during prediction. We could (and probably should) force the fallback price matrix for every toll road, however that won’t resolve the issue completely, since we want to also change the strategy how price is picked among different price matrices during prediction.

First of all, unfortunately we cannot currently group searches by session ID and it would be really difficult to implement in future, so as far as monitoring goes, we will be only able to report separate searches.

These are the metrics that can be reported during the order finish time and are generally trivial to implement:
* GMV (sum of finished order prices)
* Average multiplier
* Surge component of GMV

Median ETA is also trivial to implement, since a very similar metric already exists -- ETA histogram, it's just not possible to calculate median ETA because of the format in which metric is reported. This can be however easily fixed in code, as we're already reporting median upfront errors in the correct format, so it's a tiny change in code.

Conversion rate of searches can already be shown, since we have both metrics for number of finished orders and number of searches. The only problem here is that the time frame won't be in sync, since searches will be reported earlier than respective finished orders. If this is too much of an issue, we can calculate number of created (but not necessarily finished) orders instead at the time when they're created, which will be in sync, but will include all possible order statuses.

Driver acceptance rate of searches is similar, we just have to report drivers accepting the orders, which sounds more like a Fleet task, but isn't too hard as well.

Version of surge algorithm can be reported along with dynamic pricing metrics, but they shouldn't be relied upon as business metrics, since number of different events is more of a technical info. It is possible to report version of surge during rider searches directly, but that would require some more changes (passing DP version as a response, etc.). A side-effect of this change will be that search count won't have to be normalized, as we'll be reporting count of true rider searches as compared to aggregated count of events.

Finally, average multiplier and percentage of multipliers different from 1.0 can both be calculated during search, as well as during order finish. Calculating during order finish is trivial, calculating during search is a bit trickier, but still relatively easy.

Drivers: Which drivers? Some/all? How are they contracted (for trial but also future)? How are they classified? How are they paid? Risk of reclassification as employees? (ETC)

Providers: Who are they? How do we contract them? What are the risks/liability? How do we charge them? How do they relate to drivers? 

Invoicing: How? Who pays who? What does finance think? Does our risk of reclassification as the subsidiary get threatened?

Regarding the choice to move ahead and assume legal risks with "on-demand delivery activations", *who has approved this?* Risks are actually quite high doing something so unregulated through the use of our app. It adds to risk of reclassification of the subsidiary (a finance concern) and it also adds to the risk of reclassification of drivers as employees (because we are directing them through their use of the app far beyond the transportation service they have agreed to provide through accepting terms and conditions.) It also creates a bad rep for us as a potential food delivery agent to do this unregulated in the market, which could result in fines or even lawsuits.

I would say that even on a trial basis, the most you could do to limit this work is reduce the number of drivers and providers, but even still this will be something that needs a lot of work from multiple parties. Ken:

I'll provide below my responses to the comments made but before I would like to put this situation in context so we understand the rational behind  the decision to opt for this approach.

Basically the decision was made not to go with agency as is the case in other markets because the regulatory needs of the markets in the continent (excluding South Africa) weren't as developed and also the cost factor. An agency will be charging us minimum $4000 per country per month. 

The above situation implied we had to look for alternatives to be able to ensure regular facetime with policymakers. The instructions from Dom was that we need to do at least engagement meeting with T1 stakeholders (regulators, security etc) every quarter. Unlike the West and other more advanced bureaucratic systems, you can't just call a minister and schedule a meeting...it takes months and there is no assurance that the meeting will happen even if promised. So the need to have someone locally connected who can ensure that these meetings occur (lobbying). 


Is this agreement meant to be used again in the future on an as needed basis or was this a one-off?

The idea is that the person will help facilitate the meetings as needed. Therefore we have the generic Consultancy Agreement which defines the terms of the agreement and then we have the scope of work which is drawn up every time we contract the person to help us with getting the meetings. At this stage we are working on an $2000 fees every time they carry out the facilitation. The Consultancy Agreement has no fees specified but instead the fees will be included in the Scope of Work. 

Is "Kai Iso" the consultant's full legal name? 
Its Isa Kato as found in the Consultancy Agreement and Scope of Work

In contracting a private person it is strongly recommended to include an ID document number to clearly establish identity. 
That section of the Consultancy Agreement will be updated with ID document number and a copy of ID document included in the file

The nature of the task makes it impossible for us to set out how the consultant will go about facilitating the meetings. We have through the consultancy agreement protected Bolt from any liabilities emanating from potential corruption and bribery.

Bolt Regulatory team identifies the T1 Stakeholders that they want to meet

Hi Hannah, thanks for the prompt response.

In the industry in SA, vehicle owners need to have Passenger Liability Insurance for the vehicle to operate on our platform. However, once they are on the platform, they let their insurance lapse within months and are no longer covered.

A new law came into effect in ZA last year (the Consumer Protection Act - CPA), which basically enables consumers to litigate against anyone in the supply/value chain. This means that if something happens to a passenger on a Bolt trip, even though our Ts and Cs exclude liability, because of the CPA, they could win in court by suing Bolt for damages.

In order to protect against that, we are paying an insurer R19 per active driver per month to ensure that we aren't at risk of millions of rands in legal fees and damages.

We are then on-billing this R19 to drivers on a monthly basis (because it is a legal requirement for them). However, if the driver does more than 20 trips (for example) in a month, we will give them a R19 bonus to cover that cost.

*1. Do we have an age limit for registering as a user?*
This is rather a business question to be researched and decided then a legal one. In different markets, GDPR limits the age of consent for online registration which differs per country. Generally, companies will thus have policy higher (such as 18) to ensure that uniformly across markets this can be applied. Whether there are other regulatory considerations to take into consideration or not would also be covered with setting this at a higher age like 18. However, at the moment we do not have an age limit set in terms.

With regards to three types of liability; only type 2 is an actual requirement here (we did some more research here). Point 1, Uber requires (comprehensive commercial cover). However, it is not a legal requirement.

For individual consumers, they need to take out vehicle insurance in order to get Passenger Liability Insurance as a value add. By us taking out this fleet scheme, we can take PLi out on their behalf.

Third party insurance is not required.

*RE Roles*
Because of the Consumer Protection Act in South Africa, consumers are able to litigate anywhere in the supply/value chain for wrongdoing. This means that even though our Ts & Cs absolve us of liability, passengers could sue us for damages whilst using our service.

Because of this, I think it might be best for Taxify OÜ to be the insured party (rather than Taxify SA) but I'm happy to take your lead here.

The vehicles are only covered for Passenger Liability Insurance of they were transporting a Bolt user who requested using our app.

I've attached the FAQs (that they've approved) that we'll be putting on the blog for drivers.

The insured even is unspecified as long as it happens to the passenger whilst in a vehicle on a Bolt trip (but excluded emotional damage).

The beneficiaries are the passengers. However, they have to claim from the Road Accident Fund (RAF) in ZA before claiming from insurance.

-We notify the insurer of the number of active vehicles (those that have taken at least 1 trip in the month)

-Once the passenger has tried to claim from RAF, they can then claim from the PLi.
-At verification/claims stage, the insurer will ask for all active vehicle registration numbers in the month in question. (This is to ensure we were not under insured and to ensure that the vehicle was active).
-They will also need to look at trip logs when the claim comes in to confirm that the passenger in question was actually on a trip when the incident occurred in order to pay out to them. -This is per seat, per incident to the maximum of R5M per vehicle, per incident.

-The premium will increase as the active fleet size increases.

*RE overlap*
-There will be cases of overlap. We will no longer require PLi for new vehicles so that this should not happen in the future. We will aslo notify drivers that PLi will be covered on their trips with Bolt.
